newsitem.title: UK: GEC, BAe merger talks faltering - paper.
newsitem.headline: GEC, BAe merger talks faltering - paper.

text.p: Tentative merger talks between General Electric Co and British Aerospace are close to collapse due to disagreements on asset values and the business outlook, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The newspaper quoted one unnamed observer close to the talks as saying the chances of a merger were "very low indeed".
The Financial Times said discussions had been going on since last November but cooled over Christmas as both sides voiced reservations.
GEC chairman Lord Prior was also reported to be concerned that such a deal could face serious obstacles in the run-up to a British general election due by May.
The Financial Times said GEC had been considering a one-off payment to shareholders as part of a possible merger.
But that would have impeded its ability to finance the deal, said the paper.
The merger option was favoured by GEC's new chief executive George Simpson but finance director David Newlands was more cautious, it added.

BAe is expected to report a 75 percent increase in its full year profits after exceptional items on Wednesday, analysts said last week. Speculation about a GEC-BAe marriage has been mooted for some time.
A report in the Sunday Times said the two giants were expected to enter talks this year on forming a 16 billion stg alliance in defence equipment.

This would create the fourth biggest defence supplier in the world in an industry that is expected to witness consolidation in the coming years. The aim would be to become more competitive against U.S. rivals which are further down the rationalisation route.
